headline: FURY ADDS THIRD DRILL AS EAU CLAIRE DELIVERS 7.0 g/t AU OVER 21m — JAMES BAY HIGH-GRADE SHOOT CONFIRMED (TSX:FURY)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Fury Gold Mines Ltd.
snippet: Fury Gold Mines (TSX: FURY) announced July 13 the second batch of Phase 2 assay results from Eau Claire in Quebec's James Bay region — best hole 26EC-115 returned 7.01 g/t gold over 21.0 metres including 10.27 g/t over 11.0 metres, confirming continuity of the high-grade shoot within the modelled zone. The company simultaneously mobilized a third diamond drill rig to site, bringing the total to three active rigs and accelerating a program targeting 15,000–25,000 metres at one of Quebec's most advanced undeveloped gold deposits.

headline: MIATA'S BEST HOLE: 30m @ 4.06 g/t AU INCL. 14m @ 8.20 g/t — FOURTH 100+ GRAM-METRE AT SURINAME GOLD SYSTEM (TSXV:MMET)
snippet: Miata Metals (TSXV: MMET) reported July 13 that hole 26DDH-JT-019 at the Jons Trend target within its Sela Creek Gold Project in Suriname returned 30.0 metres at 4.06 g/t gold including 14.0 metres at 8.20 g/t gold — the best single hole drilled at Sela Creek to date and the fourth intercept exceeding 100 gram-metres from the Jons Trend–Big Berg Corridor in four months. Three of those four 100-gram-metre results have been reported in 2026 as the company works through approximately 50% of its fully funded 25,000-metre drill program, with multiple additional targets — Puma East, Big Berg, Stranger, Cambior, Golden Hand — still to receive systematic drilling.

headline: IRAN CLOSES HORMUZ 'UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE': GOLD AT $4,057 AS 4TH STRIKE IN A WEEK KILLS THE CEASEFIRE RALLY
snippet: Gold fell 1.54% to $4,057.76 on July 13 as the U.S. carried out its fourth strike against Iran in a week following attacks on shipping near the Strait of Hormuz — Iran then declared the Strait closed 'until further notice,' a claim the U.S. Central Command dismissed but oil traders did not, sending crude sharply higher and reigniting September rate-hike expectations that reversed the three-session ceasefire rally that had lifted gold toward $4,179 just hours earlier. Silver fell to $58.52, breaking below the $59 support that had held through the prior week, with both metals now awaiting Tuesday's June CPI print — the binary event that will either validate the Fed's hawkish stance or collapse it.

headline: CERRADO GOLD Q2: 15,415 GEO FROM MINERA DON NICOLAS — H1 UP 25% AS UNDERGROUND RAMP TARGETS STRONGER H2 (TSXV:CERT)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Cerrado Gold Inc.
snippet: Cerrado Gold (TSXV: CERT) reported Q2 2026 production of 15,415 gold equivalent ounces from the Minera Don Nicolas mine in Santa Cruz, Argentina — up 11.4% from 13,835 GEO in Q2 2025 — driving first-half 2026 production to 28,257 GEO, a 25.0% increase over H1 2025's 22,600 GEO. Heap leach contributed 9,981 GEO and the CIL plant 5,434 GEO in Q2; underground development is advancing ahead of plan, positioning Don Nicolas for improved ore grades and higher H2 2026 output against a gold price backdrop that generated approximately $4,100/oz realised revenue through the quarter.

headline: METAL ENERGY CLEARS FIRST DRILL AT HIGHLAND VALLEY — MULTI-YEAR PERMIT FOR BC COPPER-GOLD ON STRIKE WITH CANADA'S LARGEST CU MINE (TSXV:MERG)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Metal Energy Corp.
snippet: Metal Energy Corp. (TSXV: MERG) received a multi-year area-based Mines Act drilling permit July 13 for its Highland Valley Copper Project in south-central British Columbia — a district-scale copper-gold porphyry target on strike with Teck Resources' Highland Valley mine, Canada's largest copper producer. The permit adds a second fully drill-ready copper project to Metal Energy's portfolio alongside the NIV project, where a 6,000-metre program commenced June 29; the highland Valley permit clears the first drill hole on a target that has been explored via geophysics but never drilled.

headline: CANADA NUCLEAR PLAN: 10 NEW REACTORS BY 2040, DOUBLING URANIUM EXPORTS BY 2035 — DENISON AND NEXGEN ALREADY BUILDING
snippet: A CP24 investigation published July 13 documents the scale of Canada's nuclear revival: Ottawa has formally proposed 10 new reactors by 2040 — including an SMR at Darlington in Ontario and a Saskatchewan unit in the 2030s — and plans to double uranium exports by 2035 from the current $3 billion annual production base, all of which comes from Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin mines (Cameco's Cigar Lake and McArthur River, Orano's McClean Lake). Two companies are already in active construction: Denison Mines at Wheeler River and NexGen Energy at Rook I — representing the largest new Canadian uranium mine-development pipeline since the 1980s.

headline: TOTAL METALS ELECTROLODE HORNET ZONE: 2.90% ZN AND 1.15% CU OVER 7.67m — CRITICAL METALS SYSTEM GROWS IN NW ONTARIO (TSXV:TT)
source_name: Junior Mining Network / Total Metals Corp.
snippet: Total Metals Corp. (TSXV: TT) released the remaining results from its 8,408-metre, 25-hole winter 2026 program at the Electrolode critical metals project in northwestern Ontario, with highlight hole EL-26-013 returning 2.90% zinc and 1.15% copper over 7.67 metres with significant silver and gold credits at the Hornet Zone — a polymetallic sulphide system where multiple holes have now confirmed VMS-style mineralisation in a geological district that includes zinc, copper, silver, gold, and battery metals targets. The remaining-results release completes the winter dataset and provides the foundation for prioritising summer follow-up drilling.

headline: GOLD SUMMER DOLDRUMS '26: MID-JULY IS THE SEASONAL INFLECTION — HISTORY SHOWS 1.9% AUGUST SURGE AS AUTUMN RALLY BUILDS
snippet: Adam Hamilton's July 2026 seasonal analysis of gold's summer doldrums documents the historical inflection point: gold's weakest period runs June through early July, averaging a 0.3% June decline; but July historically delivers a 1.3% gain as institutional demand returns from summer absences, and August accelerates to a 1.9% average advance as the autumn rally gathers full momentum toward the November–December seasonal peak. With 2026's doldrums compressed into June and early July by the Iran war macro headwind, and with gold's mid-July technical setup — including COMEX net longs 13% below January's crowded peak — resembling the seasonal inflection setups that have produced the most explosive autumn rallies in the prior bull market cycle, Hamilton argues the July 14 CPI print is the catalyst that converts seasonal readiness into actual upward momentum.

headline: GOLD MID-TIERS Q1'26: RECORD 137.9% CFFO SURGE, $17.75B CASH — YET GDXJ TRADES AT 16.9x P/E, 40-QUARTER LOW
snippet: Adam Hamilton's Q1 2026 GDXJ fundamentals analysis documents the starkest valuation disconnect in modern gold mining history: mid-tier and junior gold miners delivered the sector's best quarter on record in Q1 2026 — average Q1 gold of $4,873/oz drove GDXJ top-25 cash flows from operations up 137.9% year-over-year to $7,173 million, pushing combined cash treasuries to a record $17,752 million — yet the sector's trailing P/E has collapsed to just 16.9x, the lowest reading in 40 consecutive quarters, as the January-to-July gold correction repriced equity multiples far faster than earnings deteriorated. Hamilton's framework: a sector generating record cash at record-low equity multiples represents the maximum earnings-leverage entry point of the current bull cycle for investors with conviction in the multi-year gold thesis.

headline: H2 2026 SILVER STOCK PICKS: FRESNILLO, HECLA, FIRST MAJESTIC POSITIONED AS INDUSTRIAL FLOOR HOLDS AT $58-59
snippet: Investing.com's H2 2026 precious metals stock analysis identifies Fresnillo plc, Hecla Mining, and First Majestic Silver as the three companies best-positioned to outperform in a silver recovery — backed by positive earnings revisions, strong production growth visibility, and leverage to silver's structural supply deficit (projected at 46.3 million ounces in 2026, the sixth consecutive year of shortfall) that provides a demand floor operating independently of Fed rate-hike pressure. With silver at $58.52 and testing critical support as of July 13, the analysis argues the industrial demand base from solar, EVs, and data-centre power infrastructure limits the downside risk to the $56-58 zone — and that a soft June CPI print on July 14 could trigger a catch-up move toward $65-68 in the sessions immediately following the data release.
